correctness.rationale: Using \(A_\gamma=K[y,z][x;\delta]\) with \(\delta(y)=z\) and \(\delta(z)=\gamma y\), the proof first shows \(c=x^4+\gamma x^2\) is central. Reduction modulo \(x^4=c+\gamma x^2\) makes every element uniquely cubic in \(x\). Commutation with \(y,z\) forces the \(x,x^2,x^3\) coefficients to vanish because the determinant \(\gamma(z^2+\gamma y^2)\) is nonzero. The remaining invariant ring is exactly \(K[y^2,z^2]\). PBW residues modulo exponents \((2,2,4)\) give a free rank \(16\) central module, and central localization is a central division algebra of dimension \(16\), hence PI degree \(4\).

value.rationale: The result converts the motivating paper's existence-level PI witness into the complete center and exact PI degree in a natural enveloping/Ore subfamily. The choice \(f=0\) is structurally motivated—it is the Lie/enveloping case explicitly isolated by Bell and Li—and \(\gamma\ne0\) is the nontrivial semidirect-action regime. Exact center rank and PI degree are natural invariants needed for representation-theoretic and Azumaya-locus questions, so the conclusion is more than a routine restatement of centrality.
